title: Rajkummar Rao Just Took His Shirt Off at Lord's. The Internet Lost Its Mind.
excerpt: The first poster of 'Dada: The Sourav Ganguly Story' recreates the most defiant celebration in Indian cricket — and Rajkummar looks nothing like himself.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Rajkummar Rao stars as Sourav Ganguly in the biopic 'Dada: The Sourav Ganguly Story'.
  • The film's first look was released on Ganguly's 54th birthday.
  • Rajkummar underwent extensive training to portray Ganguly authentically.
  • The biopic is directed by Vikramaditya Motwane and releases on May 14, 2027.
  • Ganguly is actively involved in shaping the film's narrative.
There is a moment that every Indian cricket fan over the age of twenty-five can describe in their sleep. July 13, 2002. The NatWest Trophy final at Lord's. India, chasing 326, on the ropes at 146 for 5, stages one of the greatest comebacks in ODI history. And as **Mohammad Kaif** flicks the winning runs, the camera cuts to the balcony, where a bare-chested **Sourav Ganguly** whips his jersey over his head and swings it like a war banner above the cricket establishment's most sacred ground. https://youtube.com/watch?v=Mo7EX4wto7s That image — furious, joyful, unapologetic — is now a poster. And the man standing shirtless against a giant tricolour isn't Ganguly. It's **Rajkummar Rao**. Dropped today on Ganguly's 54th birthday, the first look of **Dada: The Sourav Ganguly Story** is exactly the kind of reveal designed to break timelines. Directed by **Vikramaditya Motwane** and produced by Luv Films under **Bhushan Kumar's** T-Series banner, the biopic now has an official release date: **May 14, 2027**. ## The Transformation This is Rajkummar's seventh biographical role, and by all accounts, his most physically demanding. Reports say he spent months training to bat left-handed — Ganguly's trademark — and worked on mastering the ex-captain's signature off-side drives and that languid, almost aristocratic cover shot. He picked up the Bengali accent from his wife, **Patralekhaa**, a native speaker. Filming has been underway at **Eden Gardens** in Kolkata, with shoots planned in Mumbai, London, and several international locations that trace Ganguly's playing career. > **"Dropped today on Ganguly's 54th birthday, the first look of **Dada: The Sourav Ganguly Story** is exactly the kind of reveal designed to break timelines."** > "Birthdays are always special and unveiling the first look of my biopic today makes this one even more memorable. It is indeed the best birthday gift ever. Rajkummar has approached the role with great sincerity and commitment." — **Sourav Ganguly** ![Luv Films — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/71/LuvFilms1.jpg) Ganguly's endorsement isn't hollow praise. The former captain is actively involved in shaping the story, which is expected to cover his journey from the gullies of Behala to the captaincy that transformed Indian cricket's attitude overseas — the team that stopped being polite tourists and started winning abroad. ## Why This Matters for the Diaspora

For NRIs who grew up watching cricket on grainy cable feeds or gathered around laptop streams in American dorm rooms, Ganguly wasn't just a captain. He was the guy who made you feel like Indian cricket had finally grown a spine. The Lord's shirt-wave wasn't just a celebration — it was a reply to years of colonial condescension at the Home of Cricket. Every Indian kid who ever got told to calm down at a cricket viewing party understood that moment in their bones. A biopic that gets Ganguly right could do what **MS Dhoni: The Untold Story** did for a generation younger — make you feel the weight of the jersey all over again. ## The Director Makes It Interesting **Vikramaditya Motwane** is not your typical sports-biopic director. The man behind *Udaan*, *Trapped*, and *Jubilee* has a gift for making constraint feel cinematic and for finding the quiet drama in loud lives. If anyone can resist the temptation to turn Dada into a greatest-hits montage set to swelling violins, it's him.
The Legacy of Sourav Ganguly
›Ganguly's iconic shirt wave at Lord's symbolized Indian cricket's resurgence.
›He transformed India's cricketing attitude abroad.
›The biopic aims to resonate with NRIs and cricket fans.
›Ganguly's journey from Behala to captaincy is central to the film.
The film arrives just days after Rajkummar's turn as real-life prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam in *Prahaar* — two wildly different real people, introduced within weeks of each other. It's a flex that few actors in Hindi cinema could pull off. **Dada: The Sourav Ganguly Story** releases worldwide on May 14, 2027. Start practicing your shirtless balcony wave now.
